units.text: INT. NIGHT BUS - MOVING - NIGHT
The 47 night bus, half empty, yellow light flickering over torn seats and a floor sticky with old rain.
Windows fogged.
A drunk TEENAGER asleep against the glass, another one eating chips from a paper bag, a DOG on a leash tucked under a seat beside its sleeping owner.
Three in the morning is when the city tells the truth. Everyone left on this bus is running from somethin or towards it.
units.name: NARRATOR

units.text: In the back row sits RUSS DOLAN, 40s, broad, grey stubble, a gym bag between his boots he keeps touching with one foot.
Three rows ahead, NINA FALLOWS, 20s, nurses uniform under a parka, scrolls her phone with a tired thumb.
Hey. Nina. Dont turn around.
units.name: RUSS
paren: low, leaning forward, tapping the seat

units.text: Russ. Jesus. I told you, not here.
units.name: NINA

units.text: Your brother says you've got something that belongs to me. Thats all. Hand it over, and I'm off at Carver Street. No fuss.
units.name: RUSS
paren: sliding the bag with his foot

units.text: My brother says alot of things when hes scared.
units.name: NINA

units.text: Two rows up, a young man in a courier jacket, DESMOND PIKE, 30s, takes off his headphones.
He has been listening for a while.
Sorry. Is this a private conversation, or can anyone join?
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: Mind your business, pal.
units.name: RUSS

units.text: Ill try. Its difficult. This bus is only forty feet long.
units.name: DESMOND
paren: smiling, pulling out his own phone

units.text: Desmond Pike was a patient man. Desmond Pike was also a cop, and he had been following Russ Dolan for nine weeks.
units.name: NARRATOR

units.text: Across the aisle, an OLD WOMAN with a shopping trolley mutters in Polish and crosses herself.
The driver, MAUREEN, 50s, glances in the mirror and turns the radio down a notch.
Next stop Carver Street. Mind the doors please.
units.name: MAUREEN

units.text: Russ, theres a pen drive in my left pocket and its staying there. You want it, you can explain to the man in the courier jacket why.
units.name: NINA

units.text: What man.
units.name: RUSS

units.text: Hi.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: The bus brakes, hissing.
Chips-teenager drops the bag.
You wired her, did you. Her. A nurse.
units.name: RUSS

units.text: Nobodys wired, Russ. Sit down. Everyone else is going to get off at Carver, and then you and me and Nina are going to ride to the end of the line.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: No. No, I dont think we are.
units.name: RUSS

units.text: The OLD WOMAN screams.
The dog barks, the owner jerks awake.
Maureen slams the brakes and the whole bus lurches, bodies thrown, the bag skidding across the floor and spilling, not money, but a long black shape wrapped in a towel.
It always ends in the aisle. Every story on a night bus ends in the aisle.
units.name: NARRATOR

units.text: Gun! Desmond, gun!
units.name: NINA

units.text: Russ. Put it down. Put it down now.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: She took everything. Everything. You think I wanted this?
units.name: RUSS

units.text: The overhead light dies.
The bus is dark except for the streetlamps stuttering past the windows, and in the pulse of them nobody moves, nobody breathes, and the dog will not stop barking.
